_comment: Forge Framework — Complete Platform Specification v1.0. Pass this to Claude Code via --context or by placing it at the project root. This is the single authoritative spec document.

platform.name: Forge
platform.tagline: Metadata-driven, truly modular application platform for Node.js
platform.elevator_pitch: Forge is to Node.js what Frappe is to Python — but better. A Schematype (TypeScript file in git) defines your data model, validation, permissions, hooks, and UI layout. Forge auto-generates the database table, REST API, GraphQL type, TypeScript SDK, Zod validator, and Desk form — all from that one file. Every module is an independent npm package: @forge/hr never forces @forge/erp.

design_philosophy.zero_forced_dependencies: Installing @forge/hr NEVER auto-installs @forge/erp. Each module declares peerDependencies explicitly. The CLI surfaces warnings but installs NOTHING without explicit user consent.
design_philosophy.typescript_first: No any. No @ts-ignore. No JS files in src/. Schematypes generate typed SDK clients. End-to-end type safety via tRPC adapters.
design_philosophy.git_is_truth: Schematype definitions live as TypeScript files in version control. Never in a database. Schema history = git history. Schema diffs = code PRs reviewable by humans.
design_philosophy.tenant_isolation_by_design: Cross-tenant data access throws at the ORM layer. Every Redis key is auto-prefixed {site-id}:. Every BullMQ queue is namespaced. Proven by automated tests.
design_philosophy.no_floating_point_money: All currency calculations use Decimal.js. No IEEE 754 arithmetic on financial data ever.
design_philosophy.migration_never_destroys: The migration runner NEVER auto-drops columns or tables. Removal requires explicit --prune flag with double confirmation. Data safety is a hard constraint.
design_philosophy.frontend_freedom: @forge/desk is optional. Any React, Vue, Next.js, SvelteKit, or Flutter app consumes the same auto-generated APIs. No coupling.
design_philosophy.deploy_anywhere: Self-hosted: 3 commands. Cloud: 60 seconds. Hybrid: your servers managed by Forge Cloud. Identical behaviour in all modes.
design_philosophy.open_core_revenue: Everything is MIT. Money from Forge Cloud hosting (compute-based, not per-user). 25% of cloud revenue shared with marketplace app developers.
design_philosophy.windows_first_class: forge-cli works natively on Windows. No WSL. No Bash. Docker Desktop handles Postgres+Redis.

runtime.name: Node.js 20 LTS (Bun-compatible)
runtime.rationale: Single language for CLI, HTTP server, workers, and tests. No Python split-context like Frappe.

http_server.rationale: 2-3x faster than Express. Schema-based request validation built in. Plugin ecosystem.

orm.rationale: TypeScript-native, SQL-first ORM. Schema = TypeScript objects. Drizzle-kit handles migrations. Supports all target databases.

queue_names.low: {site-id}:forge:low — report generation, PDF rendering, bulk ops

cache_queue.rationale: BullMQ is the most production-proven Node.js queue. Redis for cache + queue + pub-sub in one.

realtime.room_strategy: One room per site: forge:{site-id}. Events scoped to room, zero cross-tenant broadcast possible.

tech_stack.frontend_build: Vite 5 (Rollup under the hood, fast HMR)
tech_stack.frontend_state: Zustand (global UI state) + TanStack Query (server state)
tech_stack.validation: Zod (auto-generated from Schematypes, shared between client and server)

auth.sessions: Lucia Auth (cookie-based sessions with database backend)
auth.api_keys: bcrypt-hashed, never stored plaintext, never returned after creation
auth.oauth: oslo (from Lucia ecosystem) — future: GitHub, Google, Microsoft SSO

file_storage.production: AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, or any S3-compatible

process_manager.production: PM2 with cluster mode (auto-configured by forge-cli)

testing.db_isolation: Each test file spins up isolated SQLite in-memory DB
testing.containers: testcontainers-node for integration tests needing real Postgres

cli.cross_platform: All path operations via path.join(), no shell-specific syntax

schematype_engine.description: The Schematype is the single most important concept in Forge. Everything else derives from it.

config_shape.name: string — PascalCase, unique across the workspace. Becomes the DB table name (tab{Name} convention omitted — just the name).
config_shape.module: string — npm package that owns this schema. e.g. '@forge/hr'
config_shape.label: string — human-readable name for UI display
config_shape.label_plural: string? — plural form for list views
config_shape.titleField: string — name of the field shown as the document title in links and list views

naming.description: How new document names are auto-generated

config_shape.isSubmittable: boolean? — if true, documents have Draft/Submitted/Cancelled lifecycle with beforeSubmit/afterSubmit hooks
config_shape.isSingleton: boolean? — if true, only one instance exists (like Settings doctypes)
config_shape.trackChanges: boolean? — if true, every save creates a version snapshot in _forge_versions table
config_shape.searchFields: string[]? — fields indexed for full-text search

layout.description: Optional form layout. If omitted, fields render in definition order.

sections.label: string
sections.fields: string[] — field names in this section

hooks.beforeValidate: string | HookFunction — path to module or inline function
hooks.onFormLoad: string | ClientHookFunction — runs in browser only

config_shape.workflow: string? — name of a WorkflowDefinition to attach
config_shape.printFormats: string[]? — names of PrintFormatDefinition to show
config_shape.dashboard: DashboardConfig? — charts and stats to show at top of form
config_shape.links: LinkConfig[]? — related documents to show in form sidebar
config_shape.customActions: ActionConfig[]? — buttons to add to form toolbar
config_shape.indexes: IndexConfig[]? — additional DB indexes beyond title + naming fields

options.sensitive: boolean? (never logged, never in API default response)

LongText.description: Long text. TEXT column. Optional rich text editor (TipTap).

Float.description: Decimal number. DOUBLE PRECISION column. NOT for money.

Currency.description: Money. DECIMAL(20,9) column. Uses Decimal.js in all calculations. NEVER floating point.

options.currencyField: string? — name of another field holding the currency code

Percent.description: Percentage. DECIMAL(10,5) column. UI shows 0-100 with % sign.

DateTime.description: Date + time. TIMESTAMPTZ column. Always UTC in DB, displayed in tenant timezone.

Duration.description: Duration in seconds. INTEGER column. UI shows HH:MM:SS or Xh Ym.

Select.description: Dropdown with static options. VARCHAR column.

options.options: string[] | { value: string, label: string }[] — REQUIRED
options.multiple: boolean? — multi-select, stored as JSON array

Link.description: Foreign key to another Schematype. VARCHAR column storing the target's name field.

options.fetchFields: string[]? — fields to fetch and display from linked doc

DynamicLink.description: Polymorphic FK. Two columns: one for the Schematype name, one for the document name.

options.typeField: string — name of the companion field holding the Schematype name. REQUIRED

ChildTable.description: Inline table of child documents. Creates a separate DB table with parent_id FK and idx column for ordering.

options.schema: string — name of the child Schematype. REQUIRED

Table.description: Like ChildTable but non-Schematype (lightweight, no document history).

Attach.description: File attachment. Stores S3 key as VARCHAR. Multiple option creates separate _forge_attachments rows.

AttachImage.description: Image attachment with preview. Same as Attach but UI shows image preview.

AutoName.description: The document name/ID field. Read-only. Generated by the naming strategy.

JSON.description: Arbitrary JSON. JSONB column (Postgres) / TEXT column (SQLite/MySQL).

options.schema: Zod schema string? — validate the JSON structure

Barcode.description: Barcode / QR scanner input. VARCHAR column. Desk renders scanner widget.

Geolocation.description: Latitude/longitude point. Two DECIMAL columns (lat, lng).

Password.description: Hashed password. TEXT column. bcrypt-hashed. Never returned by API.

Markdown.description: Markdown content. TEXT column. Rendered as HTML in Desk.

Code.description: Source code block. TEXT column. Syntax highlighting in Desk.

HTML.description: Raw HTML. TEXT column. Sanitized via DOMPurify before storage.

Signature.description: Digital signature. Stores as base64 PNG. TEXT column.

database_table.description: Drizzle table definition + CREATE TABLE migration SQL
details: Primary key: id UUID DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()
Name/title field as defined by titleField
idx INTEGER — for ordering within parent (ChildTable only)
parent_id UUID FK — for ChildTable relations
Index on: name, created_at, owner, parent_id (for child tables)

endpoints.GET /api/resource/{Name}: List documents. Query params: filters (JSON), fields (comma-sep), limit, offset, order_by, order_dir
endpoints.POST /api/resource/{Name}: Create document. Body: partial doc without name. Returns full doc.
endpoints.DELETE /api/resource/{Name}/{docName}: Delete document (soft delete to _forge_deleted if trackChanges=true)
endpoints.POST /api/method/{modulePath}: Call a whitelisted server function directly

rest_api.authentication: Bearer token (session or API key) in Authorization header
rest_api.permissions: Enforced on every endpoint: read/write/create/delete checked before any DB operation
rest_api.field_filtering: Hidden fields stripped from all responses for non-privileged users

trpc_adapter.description: Type-safe API client usable in Next.js or other TypeScript frontends

typescript_types.description: Generated TypeScript interfaces for each Schematype
examples: type InvoiceDoc = ForgeDoc<'Invoice'> — all fields typed
type NewInvoice = NewDoc<'Invoice'> — omits auto fields (id, created_at, etc.)
type InvoiceFilter = Filter<'Invoice'> — typed filter expressions

zod_schema.description: Zod validator generated from field definitions. Used server-side in API validation and client-side in form validation.
zod_schema.location: Auto-generated at build time, never hand-edited

desk_ui.list_view: Sortable, filterable, paginated table. Column visibility toggle. Saved filters. Bulk actions.
desk_ui.form_view: Renders from layout.sections definition. Field-level permission enforcement (read-only / hidden). Save/submit/cancel toolbar.
desk_ui.kanban_view: Drag-drop by a Select field. Auto-generated if isSubmittable or has a status field.
desk_ui.calendar_view: Auto-generated if has Date or DateTime fields.

openapi_spec.description: OpenAPI 3.1 spec. Every Schematype contributes automatically. No manual annotation.

hooks_lifecycle.description: Hooks are functions that run at defined points in a document's lifecycle. Hooks run server-side except onFormLoad and onFieldChange which run in the browser.
execution_order_on_save: 1. beforeValidate — mutate fields before validation. Good for: normalization, auto-setting defaults.
2. validate — throw ValidationError to block save. For: cross-field rules, business logic checks.
3. beforeSave — last mutation before DB write. For: compute totals, set computed fields, external API calls.
5. afterSave — post-write side effects. For: enqueue jobs, notifications, update linked docs. Do NOT throw here.
execution_order_on_submit: 1. beforeSubmit — validate submission readiness (stock available, credit limit, etc.)
3. afterSubmit — create downstream docs (GL entries, stock ledger, etc.)

hook_function_signature.server_hooks: async (doc: ForgeDoc<N>, context: ForgeContext) => void | never

hooks_lifecycle.ValidationError: throw new forge.ValidationError('Field name', 'Error message') to block save with a field-specific error
hooks_lifecycle.ForgeError: throw new forge.ForgeError('Message', 'ERROR_CODE') for non-field errors

multitenancy_design.description: One Forge process serves unlimited tenant sites. Site identity resolved from HTTP Host header at request boundary.

site_config_fields.host: string — domain name used as primary key in lookup
site_config_fields.name: string — human name (displayed in Desk header)
site_config_fields.db_url: string — PostgreSQL connection string for this tenant
site_config_fields.redis_namespace: string — prefix for all Redis keys: {namespace}:
site_config_fields.installed_modules: string[] — npm package names installed on this site

request_pipeline.step_1_nginx: Nginx terminates TLS. Preserves Host header. Proxies to Forge Fastify process.
request_pipeline.step_2_site_resolver: onRequest hook. Reads Host header. Checks Redis cache (60s TTL). Falls back to forge_sites DB table. Returns 404 for unknown hosts.
request_pipeline.step_3_context_injection: asyncLocalStorage.run({ site, db: poolManager.get(site.id), redis: nsRedis(site.redis_namespace) }, handler)
request_pipeline.step_4_auth_middleware: Validates session token or API key against the tenant's own users table. Sets ctx.user = { id, name, email, roles }. Guest routes skip this.
request_pipeline.step_5_permission_check: Every route handler calls forge.requirePermission(action, schematype) before any DB operation.
request_pipeline.step_6_route_handler: Business logic. ORM queries automatically scoped to tenant DB. No tenant arg needed anywhere.
request_pipeline.step_7_cleanup: AsyncLocalStorage context cleared automatically on request completion. Connection returned to per-tenant pool.
request_pipeline.step_8_response: Fastify serialises response. Field-level permission filter strips hidden fields.

async_local_storage_api.forge.context(): Returns current SiteContext. Synchronous. Zero overhead. Available anywhere in call stack.
async_local_storage_api.forge.db: Shorthand for forge.context().db — Drizzle connection for current tenant only
async_local_storage_api.forge.hasModule(pkg): Check if module is installed on current tenant
async_local_storage_api.forge.flag(key): Get feature flag value for current tenant

connection_pool_strategy.max_connections_per_tenant: Calculated from plan: starter=5, pro=15, enterprise=50

cache_strategy.cache_invalidation: forge.cache.del(key), forge.cache.delPattern(pattern), automatic on document save

background_jobs.context_injection: Each job receives a frozen SiteContext snapshot serialized at enqueue time
background_jobs.retry_strategy: Exponential backoff: 1s, 5s, 30s. Max 3 attempts. Dead-letter queue after exhaustion.
background_jobs.scheduled_jobs: Cron-like scheduling via BullMQ repeateable jobs. Defined in module's hookSchemas.

permission_model.description: Three-layer permission system: role-action-schematype, attribute-based conditions, and field-level rules.

permission_rule_shape.export: boolean? — can export list to CSV/Excel
permission_rule_shape.email: boolean? — can send document via email
permission_rule_shape.if_owner: boolean? — applies rule only when user is document owner
permission_rule_shape.if_condition: string? — JavaScript expression returning boolean. Context: { doc, user, site }

fields.read_only: string[]? — field names that become read-only for this role
fields.hidden: string[]? — field names hidden in API response AND Desk form
fields.no_copy: string[]? — field names excluded when duplicating a document

permission_query_hook.description: For record-level scoping (e.g. 'Sales Rep sees only own records')

permission_model.role_hierarchy: Roles are flat (not hierarchical). A user can have multiple roles. Most permissive rule wins.

forge init <name>.description: Scaffold a new Forge workspace. Runs entirely without external dependencies.

forge start.description: Start development server with hot reload
flags: --site <host>: start with a specific default site

steps: Vite build for desk + ui packages

forge site list.output: Table: host | plan | installed modules | last active | status

forge site drop <host> --confirm.description: Permanently delete a site and its database
forge site drop <host> --confirm.safety: Requires --confirm flag. Prints what will be destroyed. Waits for typed confirmation: type site name to confirm.
does: Flush Redis keys for this site

forge site backup <host>.description: Backup a site to a local or remote archive
forge site backup <host>.creates: forge-backup-{host}-{timestamp}.tar.gz containing: pg_dump.sql.gz, site.json, file manifest

forge site restore <host> <archive>.description: Restore a site from a backup archive
forge site restore <host> <archive>.behavior: Creates site if it doesn't exist. Merges if it does (--force to overwrite).

forge module install <package> [--site <.description: Install an npm package as a Forge module
flags: --site <host>: activate on specific site after install
behavior: Checks peerDependencies — prints WARNING for each unsatisfied peer dep
NEVER auto-installs peer deps — user must explicitly install them
If --site: updates sites/{host}/site.json, runs forge migrate --site {host}
Reloads server without restart (hot module registration)

forge module list [--site <host>].description: List installed modules and their activation status per site

forge module remove <package> --site <ho.description: Deactivate a module from a site
forge module remove <package> --site <ho.safety: Does NOT drop DB tables. Use forge migrate --prune after confirming no data loss.

forge migrate [--site <host>] [--dry-run.description: Diff Schemtypes against live DB and apply migrations
flags: --prune: also drop columns/tables removed from Schemtypes (DANGEROUS — requires double confirmation)
algorithm: 1. Load all registered Schemtypes (from installed modules + apps/)
3. Run drizzle-kit introspect on target DB
4. Diff: new tables → CREATE TABLE, new columns → ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, type changes → ALTER TABLE ALTER COLUMN (safe casts only), removed columns → WARNING only (unless --prune)
6. Execute in a DB transaction (rollback on any error)

forge migrate status [--site <host>].description: Show pending schema changes without applying them

forge generate schema <Name>.description: Scaffold a new Schematype file with starter template
flags: --module <path>: which package/app to create it in (prompts if omitted)

forge generate app <name>.description: Scaffold a full Forge app package

forge console [--site <host>].description: Interactive REPL with full forge context

forge setup production.description: Generate production process manager and web server config
generates: config/pm2.config.js — PM2 cluster config for HTTP + workers
config/nginx.conf — Nginx reverse proxy with all active sites
config/supervisor.conf — optional supervisor alternative to PM2

forge test [--module <n>] [--coverage].isolation: Each test file gets its own in-memory SQLite DB — no shared state, no cleanup needed

forge-framework.purpose: Primary open-source repository. All MIT-licensed packages.
forge-framework.npm_publish: All packages under @forge/* scope + forge-cli + forge-ui

branch_strategy.develop: Integration branch. All features merge here first.
branch_strategy.fix/{name}: Bug fix branches off main (for hotfixes) or develop
branch_strategy.release/{version}: Release preparation branch. Changesets PR created here.

forge-cloud.purpose: Open-source cloud control plane. Anyone can self-host Forge Cloud.
forge-cloud.relationship: Uses @forge/core as a dependency. Is itself a Forge app.

forge-agent.purpose: Installed on each managed server. Communicates with forge-cloud control plane.

starting_a_feature: pnpm test && pnpm type-check && pnpm lint
git add -p  # review each hunk before staging

releasing_packages.step_1: pnpm changeset  # describe what changed and which packages
releasing_packages.step_2: git add .changeset/*.md && git commit -m 'chore: add changeset'
releasing_packages.step_3: Push to develop → merge to main → Changesets GitHub Action creates a 'Version Packages' PR automatically
releasing_packages.step_4: Merge the 'Version Packages' PR → GitHub Action publishes to npm automatically
releasing_packages.manual_release: pnpm version-packages && pnpm build && pnpm release

multi_repo_push_strategy.description: forge-cloud and forge-agent are separate repos but may need changes in sync with forge-framework

method_git_subtree.description: Best for keeping forge-cloud as a subdirectory of forge-framework that syncs to its own repo

method_separate_checkout.description: Keep separate checkouts — simpler for independent development
workflow: # When @forge/core changes that forge-cloud depends on:
cd forge-framework && pnpm build && pnpm changeset

multi_repo_push_strategy.recommended: Use separate checkouts for forge-cloud and forge-agent. Use pnpm workspace protocol during development. Publish @forge/core to npm for cloud/agent consumption.

control_plane.name: forge-cloud
control_plane.description: The orchestrator that manages servers, sites, modules, billing, and marketplace. Built as a Forge app on @forge/core.
schemtypes: Server (cloud provider, region, IP, agent URL, status, plan)
Bench (server FK, workspace config, installed packages, nginx config)
Site (bench FK, host, plan, status, installed modules, db_url)
BackupJob (site FK, status, archive_url, size_bytes, completed_at)
DeployJob (site FK, module, version, status, log)
Subscription (site FK, plan, amount, billing_cycle, next_billing_at)

forge_agent.name: forge-agent
forge_agent.description: Lightweight Node.js REST API installed on each managed server. Receives commands from forge-cloud control plane.
forge_agent.security: All requests verified via HMAC-SHA256 signature in X-Forge-Signature header. Secret rotatable without restart.

api_endpoints.GET /health: Returns agent status, disk usage, process list
api_endpoints.POST /workspace/create: { packages: string[], docker_compose: string } → spin up Docker containers
api_endpoints.POST /workspace/update: { packages: string[], pull: boolean } → update packages, reload
api_endpoints.POST /site/create: { host: string, plan: string, modules: string[] } → create DB, migrate, add nginx vhost
api_endpoints.POST /site/drop: { host: string, backup_first: boolean } → remove site, optionally backup first
api_endpoints.POST /site/migrate: { host: string } → run pending migrations on site
api_endpoints.POST /site/backup: { host: string, upload_to: string? } → pg_dump, compress, optionally upload to S3
api_endpoints.POST /site/restore: { host: string, archive_url: string } → download archive, restore DB
api_endpoints.POST /ssl/issue: { host: string } → run certbot for Let's Encrypt cert
api_endpoints.GET /logs: { service: string, lines: number } → tail service logs
api_endpoints.GET /metrics: Returns Prometheus metrics (CPU, memory, request rates)

provisioning_flow: 1. User signs up on Forge Cloud → forge-cloud creates their Organization site
2. User chooses plan + cloud provider + region
3. forge-cloud calls cloud provider API (Hetzner/AWS/DO) to create VM
4. forge-cloud SSH-bootstraps the VM: installs Docker, installs forge-agent container
5. forge-cloud registers VM in Server schematype, stores agent URL + HMAC secret
6. forge-cloud calls agent /workspace/create to set up Docker Compose (Postgres + Redis + Nginx)
7. forge-cloud calls agent /site/create with the user's host + plan + modules
8. agent runs forge-cli commands internally to create the site
9. agent calls /ssl/issue to get Let's Encrypt cert
10. Site is live. forge-cloud updates Site.status = 'active'
11. User receives welcome email with site URL and admin credentials

submission_requirements: GitHub repository (public or private with deploy key)
Passes automated npm audit (no high/critical vulnerabilities)

forge_module_json_shape.name: string — npm package name
forge_module_json_shape.label: string — display name
forge_module_json_shape.category: string — ERP | HR | CRM | Productivity | Industry | Integration | Developer
forge_module_json_shape.schemtypes: string[] — list of Schematype names exported

revenue_sharing.free_apps: 25% of Forge Cloud hosting revenue shared with all free app publishers, proportional to installs × complexity rating
revenue_sharing.paid_apps: Stripe Connect for developers. Forge takes 15% platform fee.
revenue_sharing.rating_factors: App complexity, dependency count, support quality, update frequency

frontend_design_system.description: forge-ui: the React component library. All Forge frontends (Desk + Cloud dashboard + partner apps) use this.
design_principles: Flat surfaces only — no gradients, no shadows, no glassmorphism
Minimal borders — 0.5px, neutral color, almost invisible
Generous whitespace — components breathe, never cramped
Dark mode mandatory — every component works in both light and dark
Accessible first — WCAG 2.1 AA, keyboard navigation, screen reader labels
CSS variables for theming — never hardcode hex values
Sentence case always — no Title Case, no ALL CAPS in UI text

colors.semantic: info/success/warning/danger in background + text + border variants

design_tokens.borders: Always 0.5px — never 1px or 2px except for focus rings and accent borders

authentication_methods: API key (Bearer token in Authorization header)
session_security: Stored as bcrypt hash in DB
api_key_security: Never returned by API after initial creation
rate_limiting: 100 req/min per IP on unauthenticated routes
10 req/min on auth endpoints (brute force protection)
Per-tenant configurable overrides for enterprise plans
input_sanitization: All user input goes through Zod validation before any processing
HTML fields sanitized via DOMPurify before storage
File uploads: type validated (magic bytes + MIME), antivirus scan (optional ClamAV integration)
No eval() anywhere in codebase — enforced by ESLint rule no-eval
output_sanitization: Hidden fields stripped from API responses before serialization
Stack traces never returned to client (pino logs them server-side)
SQL error messages abstracted to generic 'database error'

at_rest: PostgreSQL: pg_crypto for column-level encryption on sensitive fields (SSN, bank accounts)
Backups: AES-256-GCM encrypted before upload to S3
File uploads: S3 server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS)
in_transit: Internal service communication (control plane → agent) via HMAC-signed requests
pii_handling: Fields marked sensitive: excluded from Pino logs automatically
PII audit log: access to sensitive fields logged with user+timestamp
Right to erasure: forge site delete + GDPR purge job implementation guide

tenant_isolation_guarantees.database: Separate PostgreSQL database per tenant. Cross-tenant SQL queries architecturally impossible through Forge API.
tenant_isolation_guarantees.redis: All keys prefixed {site-id}:. Forge Redis wrapper enforces this — raw ioredis not exposed to app code.
tenant_isolation_guarantees.files: All S3 paths prefixed forge/{site-id}/. Pre-signed URLs include scope condition.
tenant_isolation_guarantees.queues: BullMQ queues namespaced {site-id}:forge:{priority}. Workers process any tenant's queue but carry tenant context in job payload.
tenant_isolation_guarantees.realtime: Socket.io rooms scoped to {site-id}. Events cannot broadcast cross-tenant.
tenant_isolation_guarantees.jobs: Background job context snapshot includes site_id. If site_id in snapshot ≠ current tenant context, job throws immediately.
tenant_isolation_guarantees.test_coverage: Dedicated cross-tenant isolation test suite in packages/core/src/__tests__/isolation/. Must pass in CI.

dependencies.policy: pnpm audit --audit-level=moderate runs in CI. Fails build on high/critical vulnerabilities.
dependencies.updates: Dependabot configured for weekly npm + GitHub Actions updates.
dependencies.supply_chain: pnpm lockfile committed. .npmrc: prefer-frozen-lockfile=true. Provenance attestation on npm publishes.

testing_strategy.philosophy: Test-Driven Development (TDD) is mandatory. Write the test first — see it fail — then implement — see it pass. Never ship untested code.

unit_tests.db_strategy: Each test file: const { db } = createTestSite() — creates isolated in-memory SQLite DB. No cleanup needed. Zero test interdependency.
unit_tests.coverage_target: 80% minimum. 100% for permission engine and migration runner.

integration_tests.tool: Vitest + testcontainers (real Postgres + Redis in Docker)
integration_tests.coverage: Full request lifecycle: HTTP → auth → permission → hook chain → DB → response

e2e_tests.scope: Critical user journeys: login, create invoice, run payroll, submit purchase order

test_helpers.createTestSite: forge.testing.createTestSite() — creates isolated SQLite DB + test user + roles
test_helpers.createTestUser: forge.testing.createTestUser(role) — creates user with specified role in test site
test_helpers.httpClient: forge.testing.createClient(site) — Fastify inject wrapper with auth pre-configured

@forge/erp.description: Enterprise Resource Planning. Standalone — requires no other @forge/* app.

features: Double-entry bookkeeping validation on every GL posting (debit==credit or throw)
Multi-company support (one DB, scoped by company field)
Tax engine: GST India (CGST/SGST/IGST/CESS) + configurable custom taxes
Bank reconciliation: match bank statement lines to payments
P&L + Balance Sheet + Trial Balance auto-generated reports
Stock valuation: FIFO + Moving Average + AVCO

@forge/hr.description: Human Resources. Completely standalone. GL integration via optional @forge/erp peer dep.

features: Indian payroll: PF (12% basic, employer), ESI, PT, TDS (old + new regime)
Net pay calculation with all deductions
GL posting on payroll (requires @forge/erp as peer dep — optional)

revenue_sources.primary: Forge Cloud hosting — compute-based pricing (CPU/RAM/storage), NOT per-user, NOT per-module
revenue_sources.secondary: Marketplace paid apps — 15% platform fee on paid app subscriptions
revenue_sources.revenue_share: 25% of total cloud hosting revenue distributed to free app publishers on marketplace
revenue_sources.enterprise: Annual contracts: SAML SSO, audit logs, dedicated support, SLA, data residency
revenue_sources.partners: Partner credits model — partners buy credits, allocate to customer sites

pricing_principles: Never charge per user (unlike SAP, Salesforce, Zoho)
